claims.summary: For the literal r-by-r permutation-matrix CNF (O(r^3) literal length), its unique multilinear satisfaction indicator I_r is the sum of permutation point indicators, has degree<=r^2 and degree-r component perm_r (det_r in characteristic two). From a size-S depth-d circuit for I_r over k, interpolation at r^2+1 distinct elements of an extension E computes that component over E in size O((r^2+1)(S+r^2+1)), depth<=d+3. Over F2, E=F_(2^ceil(log2(r^2+1))) suffices; no binary-depth descent. In characteristic two I_r=det(M), M_ij=x_ij product_(k!=j)(1-x_ik).
claims.assessment: Working elementary indicator identity and costed interpolation, medium reviewed. Classical ingredients, novelty not claimed. Positive reduction changes field when needed; determinant-to-indicator substitution and the reverse interpolation are not an unqualified same-field equivalence.
claims.rationale: Makes the precise extraction cost in the optional canonical certificate strategy explicit; no goal-level implication changes.
claims.next_action: Retain the field distinction in the scheduled architecture comparison; no further size sweep needed.

claims.summary: There is no generic polynomial-size fixed-depth operation extracting arbitrary homogeneous components from all polynomial-size fixed-depth binary arithmetic circuits of polynomial degree. Already G_n=product(1+x_i), q=2^a, n=2q-1 has degree-q component e_q evaluating to majority, since binomial(w,q) mod2 is the a-th bit of w. Such an operation would contradict Smolensky's majority lower bound for AC0[2]. Binary constants and unbounded-fanin gates with wire size are essential.
claims.assessment: Working attributed elementary consequence of the published majority lower bound, medium reviewed. Does not rule out special component extraction with additional hypotheses or large-field interpolation.
claims.rationale: Blocks a precise unsupported binary circuit operation; this is not a new Boolean-circuit lower bound or Frege lower bound.
claims.next_action: Do not use homogeneous extraction or extension-field coefficient projection as a free bounded-depth operation.

claims.summary: Determinant polynomials over F2 have no polynomial-size fixed-depth arithmetic circuits with binary constants, by an explicit affine reduction of MOD3 to two determinants of order 2n+3 and addition of one. For A=[[0,1],[1,1]], M_i=I+x_i(A-I), the trace product detects weight not divisible by3; each diagonal entry is det([[T,b_u],[-c_u^T,0]]) for upper block-bidiagonal T with I_2 diagonal and -M_i superdiagonal. Thus universal cheap binary canonical extraction on padded permutation CNFs and cheap binary extraction of its degree-r component cannot both hold.
claims.assessment: Working explicit standard circuit-reduction consequence of Smolensky Theorem2, medium reviewed. No independent novelty. The conjunction obstruction does not identify which operation fails on the particular family; padded formulas themselves have cheap certificates. Extension constants excluded.
claims.rationale: Calibrates the optional IPS canonicalization route in exactly the binary field, without inflating a canonical polynomial's hardness into certificate hardness.
claims.next_action: Scheduled review must distinguish full-coset hardness from a source-sensitive extraction using the actual simulation image.
